SPECIAL MEETING OF THE RICHMOND CITY COUNCIL 
The Special Meeting of the Richmond City Council was called to order at 3:32 p.m. by 
Vice Mayor Doria Robinson. 
B. 
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
Vice Mayor Doria Robinson led the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
C. 
ROLL CALL 
Present: Councilmembers Jamelia Brown, Claudia Jimenez, Sue Wilson, Cesar Zepeda, 
Vice Mayor Doria Robinson, and Mayor Eduardo Martinez. Absent: Councilmember 
Soheila Bana arrived after the roll was called at 3:45 p.m.

F.1 
Budget Study Session on Proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 Operating Budget 
and Fiscal Year 2026-31 Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan and 
Department Presentations 
RECEIVE the draft Fiscal Year 2026-27 Annual Operating Budget and Fiscal 
Year 2026-31 Five-Year Capital Improvement Plan Budget presentation; 
RECEIVE updates on departmental operations and services from the following 
departments: City Attorney’s Office, City Clerk’s Office, City Manager’s Office, 
Fire and Internal Services; and upon completion of departmental presentations 
PROVIDE DIRECTION to staff prior to final budget adoption – City Manager’s 
Office/Finance Department (Shasa Curl/Emily Combs/Mubeen Qader 510-412-
2077).

Attorney James Atencio, Deputy Director of Finance Mubeen Qader, and Fire 
Chief Aaron Osorio presented a PowerPoint:  Draft Budget Department 
Presentations/Budget Updates 
(City Council took a recess at 4:29 p.m. The City Council returned from recess 
and reconvened at 4:33 p.m.) 
Interim City Attorney Shannon Moore, Deputy City Clerk Sabrina Lundy, and 
Administrative Chief Patrick Seals presented a PowerPoint:  Draft Budget 
Department Presentations/Budget Updates

and reconvened at 5:22 p.m.)

N.

N.1 
Proclamation Honoring Abigail Sims-Evelyn for Her Service and 
Contributions to Literacy and Community Uplift in Richmond 
PROCLAMATION honoring Abigail Sims-Evelyn for her compassionate 
leadership, dedicated service, and enduring contributions to literacy, learning, and 
community uplift in the City of Richmond – Mayor Eduardo Martinez (510-620-
6503). 
Deputy City Clerk Sabrina Lundy read the item into the record and noted Mayor 
Martinez, Councilmember Brown, and Councilmember Jimenez as sponsors of 
the item. Councilmember Brown introduced the item. Councilmember Brown and 
Mayor Martinez read the proclamation. The Council presented the proclamation 
to Abigail Sims-Evelyn's daughter. Ms. Sims-Evelyn's daughter, Mayor Martinez, 
and Councilmember Jimenez gave remarks. Cordell Hindler gave comments in 
person. Kevin Tisdell gave comments via teleconference. 
N.2 
Proclamation Celebrating 30 years of the Richmond United Soccer Club 
PROCLAMATION recognizing the 30th anniversary of the Richmond United 
Soccer Club, the oldest soccer organization in Richmond, and its 
multigenerational impact and role in crime reduction, pathways to career and 
educational opportunities, immigrant rights to support Richmond youth and 
families by providing access to safe, structured extracurricular activities that have 
been shown to support positive youth outcomes, including improved physical 
health, academic engagement, and social-emotional development, in crime 
reduction which led to the lowest homicide rates in the history of our City - 
Councilmember Claudia Jimenez (510-620-6565). 
Councilmember Jimenez introduced the item. Councilmember Jimenez and 
Mayor Martinez read the proclamation. The Council presented the proclamation 
to Samantha Torres on behalf of the Richmond United Soccer Club. Ms. Torres, 
Mayor Martinez, and Anderson gave remarks.  
Cordell Hindler, Anderson, Samantha Torres, and Tulio gave comments in person. 
N.3 
May is National Bike Month

residents to participate in biking events – Mayor Eduardo Martinez (510-620-
6503).

Council presented the proclamation to Maria "Downhill Diva." Maria and 
Councilmember Bana gave remarks. 
Cordell Hindler gave comments in person. 
N.4 
Proclamation Declaring May 2026 as Affordable Housing Month 
PROCLAMATION to declare the month of May 2026, as Affordable Housing 
Month in the City of Richmond to draw attention to the ongoing housing 
affordability crisis in our region and to renew the City of Richmond’s 
commitment to ensuring that all community members have safe, stable, and 
affordable places to call home - Councilmember Claudia Jimenez (510-620-
6565). 
Councilmember Jimenez introduced the item. Councilmember Jimenez and 
Mayor Martinez read the proclamation. The Council presented the proclamation

minutes_briefs.summary: Richmond City Council approved a request for the city manager to evaluate and return with recommendations within 120 days for dedicating a literacy area, department, or center in the remodeled Richmond Public Library in honor of Abigail Sims-Evelyn and her more than 40 years of service to the Literacy for Every Adult Program (LEAP).
